items.headline: Stocks claw back a sharp sell-off: Dow +0.3%, S&P 500 -0.2%, Nasdaq -0.6%
items.note: The Nasdaq was down more than 4% early Wednesday before recovering most of the loss, as AI and chip stocks fell for a second day. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen Friday for a half-day.

items.headline: Fed's favored inflation gauge hits 3.8%; traders see ~98% odds of a December hike
items.note: October PCE inflation was 3.8% over the past year, the highest since 2023, and core PCE rose to 3.3% versus the 3.2% expected. The 10-year Treasury yield still fell 7 basis points to 4.82%. A rate hike makes borrowing costlier, which tends to pressure growth and tech stocks.

items.headline: Nvidia drops about 4% for a second day; chip index falls more than 6%
items.note: Analysts said Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO on Monday did little to calm the AI trade. Micron and Sandisk were among the biggest decliners, and the Nasdaq-100 was on pace for a bear-market close.

items.headline: Anthropic closes at about $82.79, just under its $83 IPO price
items.note: The newly public AI lab is trading around its offering price as the whole AI sector swings. Large software names like Salesforce, Adobe and ServiceNow are each down roughly 25% to 60% this year, a sign of how much investors worry about AI's effect on software.

items.headline: New tariffs of up to 20% proposed on China, the EU and 12 other partners
items.note: They would stack on existing duties, pushing totals above 40% in some areas, and likely wouldn't start before January. The current US-China trade truce expires Jan. 10, so tech supply chains and chip stocks are worth watching.

items.headline: Q3 GDP revised up to a 4.3% annual growth rate
items.note: That beat the 3.5% economists expected. A strong economy is part of why the Fed is leaning toward raising rates instead of cutting. The average 30-year mortgage rate eased to 7.21% from 7.28%.

items.headline: Tech layoffs top 142,000 this year, though data roles are still in demand
items.note: One compilation citing Layoffs.fyi counts 142,000+ tech layoffs at 350 companies as of Nov. 11, but also says hiring is recovering and data science stays high-demand. It's a secondary source, so treat the figures as approximate. Data engineering and AI systems skills look strongest.

learn.explain: A tariff is a tax a government charges on imported goods. The importing company pays it at the border and usually passes some of the cost on to customers, so tariffs can push prices up and add to inflation. Today the administration proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other partners, stacked on existing duties. Investors watch tariffs because they can raise costs for companies that import parts, such as chipmakers and electronics firms, and can trigger retaliation.
learn.try: Look up which companies have said tariffs raised their costs this year, and check how their stocks reacted.
